title: Salvation and Grace - Episode 2: Ransom and justice

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome to Salvation and Grace. <short pause> I'm Jason Greene. <short pause> Tonight, we're asking how one event... <short pause> the death of Jesus... <short pause> can be described in such different ways. <long pause>

Scripture speaks of ransom and sacrifice, redemption and propitiation, as though the cross accomplished many things at once. <short pause> We're going to look at two pictures the Bible gives us... ransom, and justice... and see how they both point to the same love. <long pause>
Mark records Jesus saying something striking about his mission. <short pause>
For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister... and to give his life a ransom for many. <long pause>

A ransom is a price paid to set captives free. <short pause> In the ancient world, prisoners of war or kidnap victims could be released when the price their captors demanded was paid. <short pause> Jesus uses this image to describe his death. <short pause> He came to give his life as the payment that would release many from captivity. <long pause>
But captivity to what? <short pause>

Not to human enemies... but to sin, and its consequence, which is death. <short pause> We were held by a debt we could never pay, under a sentence we could never lift. <short pause> Jesus gave his life to pay what we owed... <short pause> and set us free. <long pause>
Now, listen to how Paul describes the same event, using the language of justice. <short pause>
For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Paul says we are justified freely by grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. <short pause>
Redemption is ransom language... the buying back of something lost. <short pause> But Paul doesn't stop there. <short pause>

Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; <short pause> to declare, I say, at this time his righteousness... that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. <long pause>

Here Paul introduces the idea of propitiation... a word that means the turning away of wrath through a sacrifice. <short pause> God set forth Jesus to demonstrate his righteousness... his justice. <short pause> In his forbearance, God had passed over sins committed before the cross, waiting for the full and final answer. <long pause>
And when Christ died, God's justice was declared. <short pause> He could be both just... <short pause> and the one who justifies anyone who has faith. <long pause>
So we have two pictures... ransom and justice... mercy and righteousness. <short pause>
How do they fit together? <short pause>

The cross is a ransom, because it sets us free from captivity to sin and death. <short pause> Jesus gave his life as the price, and we who believe are released. <long pause> But the cross is also the satisfaction of divine justice. <short pause> Sin is not overlooked, or swept aside. <short pause> God's righteousness is upheld... declared... made visible for all creation to see. <long pause>
The same blood that ransoms us... also satisfies the righteous requirements of God's law. <long pause>

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: Think of it this way. <short pause> A ransom answers the question... <short pause> what will it cost to set them free? <short pause> Justice answers the question... <short pause> how can guilt be dealt with, and righteousness maintained? <long pause>
Both questions find their answer in the death of Jesus. <short pause> He paid the price... and bore the penalty. <short pause> He released the captives... and vindicated the Judge. <long pause>
This is why the New Testament writers use so many different images. <short pause> No single picture can contain the fullness of what happened on the cross. <short pause>

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Ransom, <short pause> sacrifice, <short pause> propitiation, <short pause> reconciliation, <short pause> redemption. <long pause>
Each one opens a window onto the same astounding truth... <short pause> God has made a way for sinners to be saved. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: And because the cross is both ransom and justice, we can rest tonight in two great certainties. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: First... <short pause> you are truly free. <short pause> If you have faith in Jesus, the ransom has been paid in full. <short pause> You are no longer held captive by sin, or under the shadow of death. <short pause> The price was his life... and the receipt is his resurrection. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Second... <short pause> you stand on solid ground. <short pause> Your forgiveness is not a legal fiction, or a kindly overlooking of guilt. <short pause> God has not bent the rules, or ignored his own righteousness. <short pause> He has satisfied every requirement of justice in the death of his Son. <long pause> You are forgiven... because the debt has been paid, and the penalty has been borne. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So as you close your eyes tonight, let these truths settle around you. <long pause> The cross was enough. <short pause> It answered every question, met every demand, fulfilled every requirement. <short pause> Ransom and justice, mercy and righteousness... all meet in the love of God. <long pause>

Let's pray. <long pause> Lord Jesus, thank you for giving your life as a ransom for many... and for satisfying the justice of God on our behalf. <short pause> Help us rest tonight in the certainty that we are forgiven, free, and secure in your love. <long pause>
Goodnight.
